links.targetTitle: The same rate-limit primitive is re-expressed in each chain'

title: Keel's Solana limits are two-dimensional: Reserves cap outflow per asset, Integrations cap inflow per venue
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.2.1.3.1 defines the first axis: "`Reserve` level rate limits constrain the outflow that can occur from a given token's `Reserve` in aggregate across all Integrations." A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.2.1.3.2 defines the second: "`Integration` level rate limits constrain the flow of assets into a particular `Integration`."

Neither alone is sufficient, and the reasons are different. Integration-only limits would let Keel drain a single asset by spreading it thinly across many venues, each individually within its cap. Reserve-only limits would let the entire budget for an asset land in one venue, concentrating counterparty risk in whichever protocol the planner currently favours. Applying both means exposure is bounded per asset *and* per venue, and adding a new venue does not expand the total that asset can lose.

This is the same two-tier shape as the CCTP bridging limits — an aggregate key plus a specific key, both decremented on the same operation — reused as a general risk-budgeting idiom rather than a one-off.

The consequence for reading Keel's exposure is that no single number is the limit. The binding constraint on any given deposit is whichever of the two has less accrued capacity at that moment, so the Artifact's per-Instance limits are ceilings that the shared Reserve limit can silently make unreachable.
description: A Reserve limit constrains what can leave one token's pool across all Integrations; an Integration limit constrains what can enter one protocol — so every move is checked on both axes.
